title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DWAYNE'S WHISTLE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Dwayne Pruitt, a jet mechanic in Louisville, Kentucky.
At his Tuesday night rec league, Dwayne was the loudest man in the bleachers.
Every Tuesday, he yelled at the referee.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THROWN OUT
segments.quote: It is a general popular error to suppose the loudest complainers for the public to be the most anxious for its welfare.
segments.author: Edmund Burke
lines: One night, the ref threw him out of the gym. A fan. Thrown out.
Carl, who runs the league, followed him to the parking lot and quoted Edmund Burke, the Irish statesman:
It is a general popular error to suppose the loudest complainers for the public to be the most anxious for its welfare.
Then Carl said, We're short a ref. Prove you care.
Dwayne took the whistle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE RULEBOOK
segments.quote: Being ignorant is not so much a shame, as being unwilling to learn.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Thirty years of yelling. He figured he knew every rule.
He failed the rules quiz. Twice.
Odessa Banks, a ref for forty years, handed him a Ben Franklin line:
Being ignorant is not so much a shame, as being unwilling to learn.
So Dwayne read the rulebook at lunch, between jet engines.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HECKLER
segments.quote: When anger rises, think of the consequences.
segments.author: Confucius
lines: First game, a young guy named Tyrell yelled at every call.
Odessa's voice came back to him, a saying from Confucius:
When anger rises, think of the consequences.
So he walked over, calm, and explained the call. Tyrell blinked.
After the game, Dwayne handed him a ref sign-up sheet. Think you can do better?

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BAD CALL
segments.quote: I hold the maxim no less applicable to public than to private affairs, that honesty is always the best policy.
segments.author: George Washington
lines: Week five, Dwayne blew a call. Wrong team.
He could have just kept going. But on his break-room wall hung George Washington's words:
I hold the maxim no less applicable to public than to private affairs, that honesty is always the best policy.
He stopped the game and said, I missed it. My fault. Both coaches clapped.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: BIG LOU
segments.quote: He who dares not offend cannot be honest.
segments.author: Thomas Paine
lines: Then came the semifinal. His best buddy, Big Lou, was playing.
Lou winked at him. You got me, right, buddy?
Lou fouled. Dwayne remembered Thomas Paine:
He who dares not offend cannot be honest.
Tweet. Foul on Lou. Lou sulked a week, then bought the wings.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FINAL
segments.quote: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
segments.author: Isaac Newton
lines: On championship night, Odessa retired. Carl asked Dwayne to say a few words.
His new partner, Tyrell, grinned beside him in stripes.
Dwayne quoted Isaac Newton:
If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
Then he pointed at Odessa. She's five foot one, he said. But she's a giant. The whole gym stood up.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Help, don't holler. Learn. Cool down. Own it. Call it fair. Thank your giants.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Help instead of holler. Keep learning. Cool down. Own your mistakes. Call it fair. And thank your giants.
I tried refereeing once. I blew the whistle so hard, my glasses fell off.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
